target_customer: AI developers and companies running real-time voice and speech products that need low latency inference
problem: Real-time AI workloads need guaranteed latency and capacity, but dedicated GPU endpoints cost money while idle and serverless gives no guarantees.
business_model: Dedicated inference capacity reserved on a schedule, plus usage-based serverless streaming speech APIs

founders.name: Thomas Minassian
education: HEC Paris and University of Paris 7, Master's Applied Mathematics and Business

founders.name: Paul-Henri Biojout
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built the Yumi Dialogue Engine with 1,000 paying users and co-built Parler-TTS Mini Multilingual.

competitors.name: Deepgram
competitors.what: Streaming speech to text with Nova models and a voice agent API

competitors.name: Cartesia
competitors.what: State space model based low latency text to speech and speech to text

competitors.name: Kyutai
competitors.what: Research lab behind Moshi real-time speech to speech model

technical_complexity.rationale: A custom streaming inference engine (WPK) that keeps models in step with live input and schedules GPU capacity is hard systems work for two people.

defensibility.rationale: An efficient inference engine and capacity scheduling are hard to copy quickly, but cloud and voice vendors offer substitutes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several vendors bundled streaming speech and voice agent APIs, and LiveKit launched an inference product; the sources are undated vendor pages.

market_need_then: Voice agents were a fast growing use of AI with latency as the main complaint, per vendor and developer pages. The sources seen are mostly vendor material.

branding.domain_note: Uses dotwave.ai rather than a .com, per YC page.

identity.logo: banner with the .wave wordmark mentioned by a directory, not described

branding.brand_signature: The leading dot in the .wave name
branding.community_and_virality: Founders link to Parler-TTS, an open-source model with a reported 300,000 monthly downloads (self reported, unverified).

brand_strength.rationale: A leading punctuation mark makes the name distinctive but hard to type and search, and other brands named wave dominate results.

outcome_analysis: dotwave (.Wave) is a Winter 2025 YC company that is still active with two founders from finance and open-source speech work. No verified funding or exit was found and the YC page gives a founding year that conflicts with a directory, so no outcome can be assigned beyond continued operation.
notes: Unverified: Dealroom lists a 125k USD seed from a single paywalled page, not recorded as a round. Founding year conflicts (YC page says 2026 in one view, a directory says 2024). Competitor sources are undated vendor comparison pages; several competitors listed may have been present in 2025 but sources do not date them. Gradium raised a large seed in 2025 and is a different company.
